name: Akriai
text: Acriae or Akriai (Ancient Greek: Ἀκριαί), or Acraeae or Akraiai (Ἀκραῖαι), or Acreia or Akreia (Ἄκρεια), also spelled Acraea, was a town of ancient Laconia, on the eastern side of the Laconian bay, 30 stadia south of Helos. Strabo describes the Eurotas as flowing into the sea between Acriae and Gythium. Acriae possessed a sanctuary and a statue of the mother of the gods, which was said by the inhabitants of the town to be the most ancient in the Peloponnesus.

depictions.name: Akriai
depictions.text: Acriae Akriaia was a small village southeast of Sparta, located in the southeastern hills of Lakonia, Greece. The village was home to the perioikoi, a group of Spartan 'subcitizens' who lived in the rural communities of Lakonia and Messenia. During the Peloponnesian War the village was visited by the Spartan misthios Kassandra.
